column3: The Hebrew twice names “sons of” Simeon and calls Judah’s holding an “inheritance”; BSB condenses these expressions.
The Hebrew joins Beersheba and Sheba with “and”; BSB presents Sheba as an alternative name with “or”.
The Hebrew repeats “sons of Judah” twice and “sons of Simeon” twice; BSB varies these as Judah’s descendants and Simeonites.
The brook is “before” Jokneam; BSB specifies “east of”. The verb meaning “touch/reach” occurs twice.
The Hebrew says “eastward, toward the rising of the sun”; BSB condenses this to “eastward”.
The Hebrew repeats the direction as “eastward, eastward”; BSB uses it once.
The Hebrew has the pronoun “it”; BSB explicitly supplies Neah.
The Hebrew names Issachar twice, first separately and then as “sons of Issachar”; BSB names the tribe once.
The Hebrew says the boundary went out “to Cabul on the left”; BSB says it was “passing Cabul on the left”.
